title: Death Claims Manual: Ashgrove CareAssure Death Benefit, Interest and Payees
content:
Death claims under Asset-Based Long-Term Care Life Insurance (Ashgrove CareAssure).

## 1. Conditions of payment

1.1 Death proceeds are disbursed only on a death claim whose certified death certificate has been received and whose request status is approved, as that death claim stands on the company's record.

1.2 Disbursement proceeds only while the policy status is Death Claim Pending or Claim Paid.

1.3 A death within the contestable period of the issue date or the reinstatement date is approved only after contestable review.

1.4 A death by suicide within the suicide exclusion period of the issue date pays only premiums paid less benefits paid.

## 2. Amount

2.1 The death benefit is the specified amount less long-term care benefits paid from the acceleration pool, but never less than the residual death benefit — the lesser of the tier's residual share of the specified amount and the tier's residual cap — less installments overdue at death.

2.2 Stated as a definition: the death benefit is the higher of (a) the specified amount less the benefits paid from the acceleration pool since issue and (b) the residual death benefit, that higher amount less the ten-pay premium billed and not yet paid or waived at death.

2.3 Interest is added to the death proceeds at the tier's death-claim interest rate, simple: the proceeds multiplied by the rate and by the actual calendar days from death to disbursement, divided by 365, rounded to the cent.

## 3. Payees

3.1 Proceeds follow the beneficiary designation in effect at death.

3.2 A predeceased primary beneficiary's share passes pro rata to the surviving primaries, then to the contingents, then to the owner or the owner's estate.

3.3 A minor's share, below the minor beneficiary age, goes only to a guardian or UTMA custodian.

3.4 A payee with at least the Beneficiary Access Account minimum may elect an Ashgrove Beneficiary Access Account. Each payee's share is paid separately, by check, direct deposit or Beneficiary Access Account, the amount paid including the interest.

## 4. Record effects

Registering notice of the insured's death moves a policy that is In Force, in its Grace Period, Paid Up, Claim Active, Benefits Exhausted or on the Shortened Benefit period to Death Claim Pending. Payment of the remaining death benefit moves it to Claim Paid. A claim denied by rescission or the suicide exclusion moves it to Claim Denied, with premium refunded.

## Worked claims (hypothetical; CareAssure residual death benefit is 10 percent of the specified amount capped at $10000, interest 3.5 percent)

| Specified amount | Benefits paid from the acceleration pool | Specified amount less benefits | Residual death benefit | Higher of the two | Installments overdue at death | Death benefit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $200000 | $150000 | $50000 | $10000 | $50000 | $0 | $50000 |
| $200000 | $195000 | $5000 | $10000 | $10000 | $1200 | $8800 |
| $80000 | $80000 | $0 | $8000 | $8000 | $0 | $8000 |

Interest on the first claim, death on 1 March 2026 and disbursement on 10 April 2026: 40 actual days; $50000 multiplied by 0.035, multiplied by 40, divided by 365 is $191.78, so $50191.78 is disbursed.

Suicide within the exclusion period (hypothetical): premiums paid $24000, benefits paid $6000 — the claim pays $18000.

Pro rata passing (hypothetical): primaries A 40 percent, B 40 percent, C 20 percent; C dies before the insured. C's 20 percent passes to A and B in proportion to their shares, so each takes 50 percent. Had all three primaries predeceased, the proceeds would pass to the contingents, and with none surviving, to the owner or the owner's estate.
